paragraphs.source_en: Although they are less numerous than anthropomorphic figures, zoomorphic figures have a special position in the Round Head complex. The animals are not represented in hunting scenes, injured or dead; nor are there any scenes of reproduction or grazing. All animals are generally represented in a static position with no behavioural characteristics, which may indicate that an animal was important as an entity and not for what it did. Presuming that the Round Head art belonged to the humid period, the majority of the current wild African fauna were present in the Central Sahara at that time. However, only a very limited number of species are depicted with most animals being ignored (Table 3-2). From the very limited faunal repertoire two species are dominantly represented, namely the antelope and mouflon.

paragraphs.source_en: They are present in virtually all sites in large quantities whereas other animal species, if present at a site, are usually limited to one or just a few examples. Very rarely represented, generally not more than five each in total, are felines, insects and possible snakes. A large number of animals are not recognisable due to erosion or they were painted in too abstract a way to be identified with certainty.

paragraphs.source_en: There is a special category of animals which were represented in a particular position with their heads pointing downwards. They are usually hornless and not recognisable, as if it was a nonexistent species. It is important to say that antelope and mouflon never appear with their heads down but always up, so that the inclined position is unusual. Down-headed animals are often of large dimensions, painted in the central part of the wall in a dominant position; however, their behaviour appears rather submissive. This book introduces the hypothesis that they represent animals that did not live in the natural world but existed only in the nonreal world, such as in mythology, beliefs or dreams. These quadrupeds are treated in detail in the last chapter dealing with the interpretation of Round Head paintings.
